# Garden observations

The colour of the western bed changed after the rain. We organised the notes by plot, leaving a separate column for observations made in shade. The grey labels are still legible. A neighbour helped us carry the empty containers to the shed before the wind became stronger.

## Method

The seedlings were measured at noon because that was the only time when every volunteer could attend. The measurements may reflect differences in soil moisture; they do not establish a cause. We cannot assume that the plants nearest the wall received the same amount of light as those beside the gate. This uncertainty belongs in the report.

| Plot | Observation | Next visit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| North | Leaves remain pale | Check drainage |
| South | New growth is visible | Measure again |

Our record uses a leaf area index (LAI) to describe the canopy. LAI is a comparison within this small garden, not a promise about a commercial crop. The full method is described in the [field guide](https://example.org/field-guide). A request for the guide should include a postal address. Its response time depends on the volunteer who checks the mailbox.

## Reflection

Their going to be interviewed was unexpected. Your going to have been selected surprised the whole group. Their not going to be served immediately seemed reasonable. These remarks describe people's reactions; the possessive forms are intentional.

“Slowly, slowly,” the gardener said. Repetition is part of this quotation. We kept the wording because it captured the pace of the afternoon. The final summary should preserve the gardener's voice and the limits of our observations.[^field-note]

[^field-note]: The notebook contains estimates, not precise laboratory results.
